name: Asarfi Hospital Ltd
tagline: The only cancer hospital in the Dhanbad catchment plus a 285-bed multi-speciality unit, growing 40-50% on operating leverage post-capex and trading at ~9x EV/EBITDA vs listed-hospital peers at 15-25x - a genuine 2-4x re-rating candidate, but single-city concentration, government-receivable working capital and governance niggles keep it short of the 10x bar.
business_overview: Runs a ~285-bed super multi-speciality hospital and the Asarfi Cancer Institute (the only oncology hospital in the Dhanbad region; competitors are clustered in Ranchi) in Dhanbad, Jharkhand. NSE SME listed (IPO 2023, LM Hem Securities). Pipeline: main-board migration (2026), merger of a promoter-owned 100-bed hospital in Ballia (targeted Q1FY27), cancer-hospital expansion of +150-200 beds (unlocks a ~Rs 12.5 Cr Jharkhand subsidy), and an education / nursing-college leg. Seeded via forum discovery; theme match - single-speciality hospitals & diagnostics (priority 2).
fundamentals_table: +48.9% to Rs 128 Cr FY25; H1FY26 Rs 80.6 Cr (+50% YoY)
EBITDA Rs 15.86 Cr (~20% margin); PAT Rs 7.32 Cr (+70% YoY, ~9% margin)
D/E ~0.4 - modest; small term loans for cancer-unit / education build
High receivables - ~50% of revenue is government schemes (Ayushman Bharat, CGHS, Coal India, Railways)
fundamentals_narrative: Asarfi is a small regional hospital showing textbook post-capex operating leverage: FY25 revenue +49%, H1FY26 revenue +50% and PAT +70%, EBITDA margin ~20%, ROCE ~20%, driven by rising occupancy and IPD volumes plus a small ARPOB uptick (pricing headroom in Dhanbad is limited). Its structural edge is geography - it is the only cancer hospital in a large, under-served eastern catchment, with the nearest serious alternatives far away in Ranchi or West Bengal. Trading at ~9x EV/EBITDA against listed hospitals at 15-25x, there is a clear re-rating gap. The constraints: a single-city footprint, working capital hostage to government-scheme receivables, and a set of governance niggles (audit trail not enabled for two years, NABH accreditation only entry-level despite website claims, related-party transactions with promoter entities, a young promoter with no medical background - the CFO effectively runs it, and a land-title dispute on the cancer-hospital plot sent back for fresh adjudication).
technical_read: NSE SME; corrected ~40% from the top despite strong FY26 numbers (one session hit a 20% lower circuit). Not pulled in detail - SME liquidity distortions dominate the chart.
sentiment_summary: ValuePickr thread 107868 - 20 posts, first-time read. @Agni (not a trusted user) is the primary tracker: thorough, invested, cautiously positive; has repeatedly written to the company and published management replies (the Rs 18 Cr 'loans' turned out to be a Ranchi land advance + subsidiary funding; ARPOB-formula discrepancy resolved; NABH is entry-level only). Concerns raised in-thread: government-receivable-heavy working capital, single-city concentration, RPT with promoter's ASAP Impact and a separate Asarfi Ballia hospital held outside the listco (now proposed for merger), audit trail not enabled two years running, promoter depth. @Satishwe (trusted, elevated) posted once (Feb-2026) relaying '40% topline growth for Q3' - a positive datapoint, not a full call. Recent posts debate value-buy vs value-trap after the 40% correction; one poster cites a replacement-value floor of ~Rs 600-800 Cr.
community_signal: Constructive but not high-conviction. One trusted-user (@Satishwe) results relay (mild positive). Main tracker @Agni (non-trusted) is invested and positive but openly lists governance niggles.

trusted_signals.note: Relayed '40% top-line growth for Q3' with results image (love 4). A positive results datapoint from a trusted (elevated) user, not a full conviction call.

bse_notes: No SEBI / fraud action. Governance monitorables (from the VP thread / annual report, none rising to HIGH CAUTION): statutory audit trail not enabled for two consecutive years; NABH accreditation only entry-level while the website implied full; related-party transactions with promoter entities (ASAP Impact) and a promoter-owned hospital (Asarfi Ballia) outside the listed entity now proposed for an equity-swap merger; promoter (MD) is young with no medical background - CFO runs operations; land-title dispute on the cancer-hospital plot remitted for fresh adjudication. Working capital is structurally stretched by government-scheme receivables.
bull_case: Only cancer hospital in a large, under-served Dhanbad / eastern catchment - a genuine local moat
Post-capex operating leverage: FY25 revenue +49%, H1FY26 revenue +50% / PAT +70%, EBITDA margin ~20%
~9x EV/EBITDA vs listed hospital peers 15-25x - clear re-rating gap
Multiple near-term triggers: main-board migration, Ballia hospital merger (Q1FY27), cancer-unit expansion + Rs 12.5 Cr subsidy, Gleneagles multi-organ-transplant tie-up
bear_case: Single-city footprint - the 1,000-bed / O&M 10-year vision is entirely unproven
Working capital hostage to government-scheme receivables (~50% of revenue); negative operating cash flow in a past year
Governance niggles: audit trail not enabled 2 years, entry-level-only NABH, promoter RPTs, young non-medical promoter
Local moat erodes as competitors add oncology / super-speciality beds in tier-1/2 cities
Asset-heavy expansion; funding mix for Ballia merger + cancer-unit build not settled
NSE SME liquidity; stock already corrected ~40% - value-trap risk cited on-thread
10x needs ~10x earnings or a huge re-rate - the realistic path is a 2-4x re-rate, below the screen's bar
verdict_headline: Real operating leverage, a genuine local oncology moat and a wide valuation gap vs peers - a solid ~2-4x re-rating candidate, but single-city concentration + government-receivable working capital + governance niggles put it short of the 10x/100x bar. thesis_fit 'neither', conviction Low-Medium.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind yes (structurally under-served tier-2/3 healthcare + oncology penetration in eastern India), tam weak (single-city footprint today; regional replication / O&M model is unproven and is the swing factor), moat weak (only cancer hospital in the catchment is a real local moat but erodes as beds are added elsewhere; asset-heavy), valuation weak (~9x EV/EBITDA is genuinely cheaper than peers, but SME discount + governance niggles keep it 'weak' not 'yes') -> score 2.5

Score 2.0-2.5: the un-ignorable-growth carve-out was considered (40-50% topline, 70% PAT, operating leverage) but the honest return-magnitude read is a 2-4x re-rate-plus-earnings-growth path, not 10x in 2-3 years - so thesis_fit is set to 'neither' rather than forcing a capped return-magnitude label. The re-rating upside is noted in the write-up.

Conviction Low-Medium: strong recent execution + a genuine local moat + a cheap multiple keep it off Low; single-city concentration, government-receivable working capital, and the governance niggles cap it below Medium
Theme match: single-speciality hospitals & diagnostics (priority 2) - value_chain block seeded from the theme
Trusted signal: @Satishwe (elevated) results relay logged as a mild positive; primary tracker @Agni is non-trusted
No red-flag tier - the audit-trail / NABH / RPT items are monitorables, not a promoter-holding collapse or auditor resignation

four_box.note: tam weak (single-city footprint; regional replication unproven) is the binding box. moat weak (local oncology moat real but erodes with new beds; asset-heavy), valuation weak (~9x EV/EBITDA cheap vs peers but SME + governance discount). tailwind yes (under-served eastern-India healthcare / oncology). Realistic path is a 2-4x re-rate, not 10x -> thesis_fit 'neither'.

value_chain.position: Regional multi-speciality + dedicated oncology hospital in an under-served eastern-India (Dhanbad) catchment; government-scheme heavy payer mix
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Oncology / super-speciality bed capacity in the local catchment - Asarfi is currently the only provider
value_chain.note: Local supply is thin (a real near-term moat) but the medium-term risk is other operators adding oncology / super-speciality beds in tier-1/2 cities; the ROCE turn is visible in FY25-26 (post-capex operating leverage), payer mix (government schemes) is the working-capital drag.
